framework: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 (incident response, aligned to CSF 2.0) and the CISA #StopRansomware Guide, simplified for non-technical SME owners.
reviewNote: Pre-vetted content. The AI may rephrase these steps but may never add, remove or reorder them. Have a qualified professional review before production use.

escalation.title: Get a human expert

contacts.name: Your IT vendor / managed service provider
contacts.detail: Use the number on your support contract

escalation.preserveEvidence: Until an expert arrives: keep the affected computer switched ON but disconnected from the network, and do not delete anything. Memory (RAM) holds evidence that is lost on shutdown.

ransomware.name: Ransomware
ransomware.plainName: Your files are being locked by criminals who will demand payment
doNot: Do not switch the computer off or restart it.
Do not pay or reply to the criminals before speaking to an expert.
Do not plug backup drives into any computer.

containment.title: Cut the network
containment.instruction: Pull the network (ethernet) cable out of {deviceId} and switch its Wi-Fi off.
containment.why: The locking spreads through the network to other PCs and shared folders. No connection, no spread.

containment.title: Leave it switched on
containment.instruction: Leave {deviceId} switched ON. Do not restart it or close any windows.
containment.why: The key to unlock your files sometimes sits in the computer's memory, and it vanishes if you turn it off.

containment.title: Protect your backups
containment.instruction: Unplug any backup drive or shared storage box (NAS) from the network and from every computer.
containment.why: Ransomware hunts for backups first so you have no choice but to pay.

containment.title: Warn your team
containment.instruction: Tell everyone to stop using shared folders and not to open files until you give the all-clear.
containment.why: Opening a locked file on another PC can spread the problem.

containment.title: Record the evidence
containment.instruction: Take a phone photo of any ransom message on screen. Do not reply to it.
containment.why: Investigators and insurers need it, and the message often identifies the gang.

learn.analogy: It is like a burglar who does not steal your filing cabinet but snaps their own padlock on it, then offers to sell you the key.
learn.howItHappened: Criminals usually get in through a fake email attachment, a stolen password, or an unprotected remote-access connection. Once inside, a program quietly locks every file it can reach and leaves a note.
learn.businessImpact: Invoices, payroll and customer records become unusable until they are restored. Paying does not guarantee you get them back.

prevent.title: Daily offline backups
prevent.description: Back up every night to storage that is disconnected afterwards, so criminals cannot reach it.

prevent.title: Two-step login for everyone
prevent.description: A stolen password alone will no longer get anyone in.

prevent.title: Automatic security updates
prevent.description: Close the known holes criminals scan for every day.

brute_force.name: Password-guessing attack
brute_force.plainName: Someone is trying thousands of passwords to break into an account
doNot: Do not reuse the old password anywhere.
Do not change passwords from the computer being attacked.

containment.title: Change the password
containment.instruction: Using a different, trusted device (e.g. your phone), change the password of the account being attacked. Make it a long phrase you have never used.
containment.why: If they already guessed it, this locks them back out.

containment.title: Kick out other sessions
containment.instruction: In that account's security settings, choose 'Sign out of all sessions' (Google: 'Sign out everywhere'; Microsoft 365: 'Sign out everywhere').
containment.why: Anyone already logged in stays logged in until you do this, even after a password change.

containment.title: Block the attacker
containment.instruction: Ask your IT vendor to block {sourceIp} on your router or firewall. If no one is available, pull the network cable out of {deviceId} for now.
containment.why: This stops the guessing at the door.

containment.title: Look for changes
containment.instruction: Check the account for anything you did not do: new email forwarding rules, new users, changed bank details or sent emails.
containment.why: Attackers often set up a quiet email forward to keep spying after they are locked out.

learn.analogy: It is like someone standing at your shop door trying every key on a giant key ring, very fast, all night.
learn.howItHappened: Automated tools try common and leaked passwords against any login that faces the internet, such as email, remote desktop or the shop system.
learn.businessImpact: One correct guess gives them your email, customer data and the ability to send fake invoices in your name.

prevent.title: Two-step login for everyone
prevent.description: Even a correct password guess is useless without the code on your phone.

prevent.title: Lock accounts after 5 wrong tries
prevent.description: Turns a million guesses into five.

prevent.title: Block this attacker for good
prevent.description: Add {sourceIp} to your permanent firewall blocklist.

suspicious_ip.name: Connection to a criminal server
suspicious_ip.plainName: A computer is talking to an address known to be used by criminals
doNot: Do not switch the computer off.
Do not log in to banking or email from that computer.

containment.title: Cut the network
containment.instruction: Pull the network cable out of {deviceId} and switch its Wi-Fi off.
containment.why: This stops the hidden program from receiving orders or sending your data out.

containment.title: Leave it switched on
containment.instruction: Keep {deviceId} switched ON and do not restart it.
containment.why: Experts can see what the program is doing only while it is still running in memory.

containment.title: Remember what happened
containment.instruction: Write down what the person using {deviceId} did today: emails opened, links clicked, files downloaded, USB sticks used.
containment.why: It tells us how the program got in, so it does not happen again.

containment.title: Change passwords elsewhere
containment.instruction: From a different, trusted device, change the passwords for email and banking that were used on {deviceId}.
containment.why: Hidden programs often record what you type.

learn.analogy: It is like finding out one of your office phones has been secretly dialling a criminal's number every few minutes to ask for instructions.
learn.howItHappened: A hidden program, usually from an email attachment or fake download, was phoning home to a server the criminals control.
learn.businessImpact: The criminals can watch, steal files or install ransomware later, at a time that suits them.

prevent.title: Block the criminal server
prevent.description: Add {sourceIp} to your firewall blocklist so no PC can reach it again.

prevent.title: Protection on every PC
prevent.description: Install business antivirus (endpoint protection) that blocks known bad programs.

prevent.title: 5-minute staff lesson
prevent.description: Teach the team to spot fake emails and downloads.

data_exfiltration.name: Data being stolen
data_exfiltration.plainName: A large amount of your data is being sent out of the business
doNot: Do not delete logs or files to 'clean up'.
Do not contact customers before you know what was taken.

containment.title: Cut the network
containment.instruction: Pull the network cable out of {deviceId} and switch its Wi-Fi off.
containment.why: Every second connected, more data leaves.

containment.title: Leave it switched on
containment.instruction: Keep {deviceId} switched ON and do not restart it.
containment.why: The record of what was sent and where is still in memory.

containment.title: List what was on it
containment.instruction: Write down what kind of data {deviceId} could reach: customer lists, IC numbers, payroll, card details, contracts.
containment.why: This decides who you may legally need to inform.

containment.title: Start the legal clock
containment.instruction: Note the time now. If personal data was involved, Malaysia's PDPA may require you to notify the Personal Data Protection Commissioner within 72 hours. Call your advisor or Cyber999 today.
containment.why: Missing the deadline can bring penalties on top of the breach itself.

learn.analogy: It is like noticing a delivery van backing up to your stockroom at midnight and loading boxes you never sold.
learn.howItHappened: Someone with access, either a criminal using stolen login details or hidden software, copied files and uploaded them to an outside server.
learn.businessImpact: Stolen customer data can lead to fines, lost trust and blackmail threats to publish it.

prevent.title: Alerts on big uploads
prevent.description: Get a phone alert whenever unusually large amounts of data leave the office.

prevent.title: Two-step login for everyone
prevent.description: Stolen passwords stop being enough to get at your data.

prevent.title: Need-to-know access
prevent.description: Staff only get the folders their job needs, so one breach exposes less.

universal.name: Unrecognised threat
universal.plainName: Something unusual and serious happened that does not match a known attack
references: CISA guidance: isolate, preserve volatile memory, escalate
doNot: Do not switch the computer off or restart it. Memory holds evidence.
Do not try to 'fix' it by deleting files or running cleaner tools.
Do not log in to other accounts from that computer.

containment.title: Cut the network
containment.instruction: Pull the network cable out of {deviceId} and switch its Wi-Fi off.
containment.why: Whatever it is, disconnecting stops it spreading or calling home. This is safe for every type of attack.

containment.title: Preserve the evidence
containment.instruction: Keep {deviceId} switched ON and plugged into power. Do not restart, sleep or log out.
containment.why: The computer's memory (RAM) holds clues that disappear the moment it powers off. Experts need it to identify unknown threats.

containment.title: Write down what you saw
containment.instruction: Note the time, what was on screen, and anything odd staff noticed in the last day (pop-ups, slowness, strange emails).
containment.why: Small details help experts work out what happened much faster.

containment.title: Call an expert
containment.instruction: Press 'Escalate to a human expert' below and contact Cyber999 or your IT vendor. Unknown threats need a professional to look at the machine.
containment.why: We could not match this to a known attack, so a person must investigate before it is used again.

learn.analogy: It is like a smoke alarm going off with no obvious fire: you get people out and call the fire brigade before you go hunting for the cause.
learn.howItHappened: The sensor saw a critical event, such as security logs being wiped or a system component being tampered with, that does not match a known attack pattern.
learn.businessImpact: Unknown problems can be the early sign of a serious attack. Treating it seriously now is far cheaper than recovering later.

prevent.title: Protection on every PC
prevent.description: Business antivirus that detects and blocks suspicious behaviour automatically.

prevent.title: Automatic security updates
prevent.description: Close known holes before criminals use them.

prevent.title: Daily offline backups
prevent.description: Whatever happens next, you can restore your business.
